name: Launchboard
tagline: A dashboard for planning a product launch and tracking submissions to directories, communities, and press.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The interface here is a board: statuses, dates, links, notes, a checklist per destination. That part is close to a solved problem for a coding agent, and a local SQLite app will do it in an afternoon. The thing you cannot generate is the curated list of places worth launching on, with their actual submission rules, fees, review times, and whether they still exist. Most of the paid value in this category is that list staying current, not the columns it sits in. Build the board, then accept that you are now the one maintaining the list.
coreLoopDIY: A local kanban of launch destinations with per-destination fields, checklists, due dates, and a status pipeline you move cards through.
requirements: somewhere to keep a SQLite file
your own list of directories and communities to seed it with
whatYouLose: A maintained, deduped directory list with live URLs and current submission requirements
Any sense of which launch venues actually drive traffic versus which are dead link farms
Prewritten copy templates sized to each destination's character limits
Reminders and scheduling that nag you without you opening the app
Multi-product or client-facing views if you launch things for other people
moatNotes: The research work is the product. Link rot in launch directories is brutal and a stale list is worse than no list.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because launching is a one-week panic, not an ongoing habit, and nobody wants to spend day one of that week googling which of forty directories still accept submissions. Paying for a current list and a place to track sixty checkboxes is a rational trade during the exact window you have no attention to spare. The month after launch, the subscription is dead weight, which is why tools like this tend to get bought, used hard, and cancelled.
notes: The board is trivial, the list is the asset · budget an evening for the app and a weekend for the research it replaces.
prompt:
Build a local-first launch tracker called "launchboard-local". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind. No component library.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/launchboard.db, created and migrated on first boot.
- Server actions for all writes. No separate API layer, no client state library.

Data model:
- product: id, name, url, one_liner, notes.
- destination: id, product_id, name, url, kind (directory | community | press | newsletter | podcast | other), status (backlog | drafting | submitted | live | rejected | dead), fee_cents, submitted_at, live_at, live_url, notes, priority (1-3).
- task: id, destination_id, label, done. Seeded per destination from a template list.
- asset: id, product_id, label, body. For reusable blurbs, e.g. "60 char tagline", "280 char post".

UI:
- / : board view, one column per status, cards show destination name, kind badge, fee, priority dot. Drag to change status, or a status dropdown if drag is getting long. Keyboard: "n" opens new destination.
- /d/[id] : destination detail with all fields editable inline, checklist, a notes textarea that autosaves, and a copy button next to each product asset.
- /assets : CRUD for reusable blurbs, each showing a live character count.
- Top bar: product switcher, plus counts by status and total fees spent.

In scope: CSV import of destinations (name,url,kind,fee), CSV export of everything, a "stale" flag on any card sitting in drafting or submitted for more than 14 days.

Out of scope: auth, email, scraping directory sites, any bundled list of directories, integrations, mobile app, multi-user.

Seed the db with one example product and three example destinations so the board is not empty on first run. Ship a README with setup in four commands and a .env.example holding only PORT. Commit nothing to ./data.
